aboutIntro: Software developer and Fatec Cotia graduate. My interests range from how systems work to the experience of the people who use them.
aboutParagraphs: I started with an interest in making games, first trying Lua for Roblox, then learning Python through the Ignorância Zero channel. I made Pygame games. Discovering Django led me to HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Git and web development tools.

Python remained my tool for scripts, command-line utilities and exercises. At college I discovered CentOS and switched my personal computer to Ubuntu. I explored networking, servers, Docker, cloud and automation with Ansible, Terraform and Vagrant.

Linux became a key interest. I explored Ubuntu, RHEL, CentOS, Alpine, AlmaLinux, Fedora and Arch, alongside shell, permissions, firewalls, web servers and virtual-machine labs. I am studying for LPIC-1 and deepening my networking knowledge.

Wanting to understand how things work led me to Rust, my favorite language. I created Textforge, a small language for batch text processing through descriptive pipelines, published on crates.io. Python and Node.js bindings are in development.
During my Fatec internship I worked on an asset and inventory management system with TypeScript, NestJS and React, accompanied by a Kotlin barcode-scanning app.

I also explored AI-assisted development in a GNS3 fork, using incremental specifications, code reviews and corrections. I worked on zoom, images, device grouping, text and geometric shapes. I am also working on a Rust RFC proposal for partial impl blocks.

On Redlint, now inactive, I published over 150 shorts explaining IT concepts directly. I continue learning through courses, documentation and projects, with an interest in testing, documentation, security and open-source contribution.

inventario-fatec.description: Asset and inventory management system I built during my internship for Fatec Cotia. It replaces the state-issued spreadsheet and a makeshift barcode reader with a NestJS API backed by PostgreSQL, a React portal and a Kotlin Android app that scans labels with the camera and works offline.
inventario-fatec.successes: Imports the institutional spreadsheet while keeping its identifiers, and shows differences field by field so the staff decide what to keep on every re-import. The app runs room-by-room inventories with an offline queue (SQLite + WorkManager) and detects version conflicts instead of overwriting data. Every step of an asset's life is recorded: incorporated, checked, made available with a photo and a condition score, reserved, shipped and transferred, or sent for write-off after 20 days with no takers, with e-mail notices. It also has per-task permissions with session revocation, bulk changes with undo and redo, CSV, XLSX and ODS reports, a documented security review, CI tests against a real PostgreSQL database, and a guided installer for Windows or Linux with a signed APK.
inventario-fatec.failures: The final deployment still depends on the college: the system currently runs over HTTP on the local network, and HTTPS, a real SMTP server and the backup routine must be set up by the institution. Camera scanning still needs to be validated with the real labels and phones. Inventories must be prepared online before entering a room, there is no password recovery by e-mail and no PDF reports, and spreadsheets are parsed synchronously with a 10,000-row limit per file; larger databases will need background processing.

api-php.description: Online store and admin panel for a fictional building-materials company: a REST API in plain PHP 8 with Propel and MySQL, a React + TypeScript frontend and a full Docker setup.
api-php.successes: Framework-free REST API covering products, stock, categories, discounts, customers, carts, orders, sellers and addresses, with API-key authentication and per-admin CRUD permissions. The React store and admin panel use every route, the store key stays hidden behind the NGINX proxy, and an end-to-end test checks 141 scenarios. It starts with a single docker compose up, demo data included.
api-php.failures: The first version had serious flaws, such as plain-text passwords, hashes exposed in responses and files reachable without a key; 30 fixes followed, all documented. Still to do: speed up key validation, which checks the key against every admin's hash and makes each request take about 1 s, and apply catalog discounts in the cart as well.
